root_idea.summary: The supplied evidence centers on provision of sufficiency through retained possessions, with a related extension to contentment.
root_idea.development: The Quran-focused discussion connects قِنْيَة with saved wealth and also interprets the Quranic expression as granting رضا وطاعة, described as a higher form of sufficiency. This development is supported by the Quran-focused lexical discussion, not by an independent root-principle source.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The sole Quran-attested form is retained as a public entry in normalized Arabic orthography.

senses.definition: To provide what gives sufficiency, specifically retained or stored wealth (qinyah).
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic pairing أَغْنَىٰ وَأَقْنَىٰ, this is explained as granting what contains sufficiency and what constitutes qinyah, namely saved wealth.
A further interpretation of the same Quranic expression understands the granted qinyah figuratively as رضا وطاعة, contentment and obedience.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To acquire, possess, or retain something as a possession.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited Classical forms include acquiring or keeping a thing and figuratively retaining such qualities as modesty; this is broader than the Quranic causative use.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer-only unit: it only says to see قنو and supplies no lexical definition.

cautions: The supplied QAC record labels أَقْنَىٰ as a noun, while the Quran-focused lexical discussion explains the form through the verbal interpretations of granting qinyah and satisfying; the public POS label follows the supplied QAC morphology.
